ai.description: The Yunnan keelback reaches 60–80 cm. It is olive-brown with a distinct yellow nuchal collar and dark lateral spots. Keeled scales and a dark subocular streak distinguish this Natricidae species.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Hebius clerki* is best distinguished by the distinct, pale, V-shaped or chevron-like marking on the nape, which is absent in most other similar Indian keelbacks.
ai.habitat: *Hebius clerki* inhabits high-altitude montane forests and grassy meadows in the Himalayas, typically found near streams at elevations between 2,000 and 3,000 meters.
ai.behavior: The Yunnan keelback is primarily diurnal, actively foraging for small amphibians like frogs and tadpoles in or near mountain streams during the day.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Hebius clerki* is oviparous, laying clutches of 3–8 eggs. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, typically between June and August in its Indian range.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Yunnan keelback occurs in Northeast India, specifically in Arunachal Pradesh and Nagaland, typically inhabiting mid-to-high elevation forests in the Eastern Himalayas.
